rationale: The route USER→WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP correctly represents the requested conjunction: admin role lives on WORKSPACE_MEMBERSHIP while title lives on USER, and both conditions target the same person (Robert Walsh), matching resolution_mode 'single'. The design's negatives are well-chosen and non-trivial: another admin with the wrong title, a non-admin member with the matching title, and a plain member failing both conditions — this prevents a solver from succeeding via a single-field shortcut (role-only or title-only filtering). The title values for the relevant users are absent from the shown base_seed sample but are legitimately new rows the compiler is expected to add per the design (consistent with the note that planned additions need not preexist in the seed), and they are consistent with the existing user_teams role assignments (Robert/Morgan admin, Nick/Artem member) already present in the seed. Access via users.list + users.info is plausible: the domain model states owner/admin flags derive from the stored membership role and title is an ordinary stored user column, so no hidden-field or unsupported-capability problem arises. Answer attributes (email, title, real_name) are legitimate bare columns. The prompt is a short, realistic ask with a consequential-enough single answer and does not hint at the answer. No mechanical or referent-entity errors are evident.
